summary.title: Readings in Database Systems, 5th Edition
summary.one_liner: A curated collection of classic and modern database research papers, each introduced by a leading researcher, spanning traditional RDBMS, new architectures, dataflow engines, weak isolation, query optimization, and interactive analytics.
takeaways: Get a guided reading list of classic and recent data management research
See which topics the edition covers: RDBMS, new architectures, dataflow engines, weak isolation and distribution, query optimization, interactive analytics
Find each chapter's introducer: Michael Stonebraker, Peter Bailis, or Joe Hellerstein
Each chapter is available in HTML and PDF form
summary.summary: The page is the front page of the Fifth Edition of Readings in Database Systems, known as the "Red Book", a long-running opinionated reading list in data management first published in 1988. It lists the chapters, each with a short introduction by one of three named authors (Michael Stonebraker, Peter Bailis, Joe Hellerstein) and links to HTML and PDF versions. Topics run from a background chapter and traditional RDBMS systems through techniques everyone should know, new DBMS architectures, large-scale dataflow engines, weak isolation and distribution, query optimization, and interactive analytics. The page itself contains no further detail on the readings beyond the chapter list.
